name: Crypto basis trading
heading: The Structural Opportunity: Futures Premium Over Spot
caseLead: Crypto basis trading earns the premium between futures and spot prices by buying the underlying asset and selling the futures contract. The premium reflects demand for leveraged long exposure and can persist when exchange credit limits, funding costs or regulatory barriers restrict arbitrage.
caseRest: The main risk is failure of the exchange or custodian holding the assets and collateral, which can invalidate an otherwise hedged position. In November 2022 the failure of FTX showed that collateral held on a venue can be frozen even when both legs of the trade are correctly hedged. A second risk is that the premium falls to zero in a sell-off, which leaves little return for the capital tied up, while forced liquidation of one leg during a sharp move can cause losses on the other.
figNote: Each card shows the change in the price of bitcoin over the month of the episode. A rise lifts demand for leveraged long positions and widens the futures premium, while a fall narrows it and can trigger forced liquidations.

events.title: Covid sell-off forces leveraged exchange liquidations
events.text: Bitcoin fell by more than a third on 12 March 2020 as investors sold to raise cash, and it ended the month 25% lower. The strategy lost because exchanges liquidated leveraged positions and the futures premium disappeared, so margin calls forced closing at a loss.

events.title: Institutional buying lifts bitcoin to record highs
events.text: Bitcoin rose 47% in December 2020 as institutions and payment companies increased purchases, passing its 2017 high of about $20,000. The strategy gained because demand for leveraged long positions pushed the futures premium well above the cost of cash.

events.title: China mining ban triggers heavy liquidations
events.text: Bitcoin fell 35% in May 2021 after Chinese authorities moved against mining and crypto services and Tesla suspended bitcoin payments. The strategy lost because liquidations on offshore exchanges cut the futures premium and forced leveraged traders to close positions.

events.title: FTX collapse exposes counterparty risk
events.text: Bitcoin fell 16% in November 2022 as the exchange FTX filed for bankruptcy and froze customer withdrawals. The strategy lost because collateral held on the exchange became inaccessible, and funds had to close hedges at wider spreads on other venues.

events.title: Spot bitcoin ETF inflows widen the futures premium
events.text: Bitcoin rose 16% in March 2024 to a record near $73,000 after US spot bitcoin ETFs, approved in January, drew steady inflows. The strategy gained because demand for leveraged long positions lifted the futures premium to its highest level in about three years.

events.title: US tariffs test the futures premium
events.text: Bitcoin fell below $75,000 on 7 April 2025 after the announcement of US tariffs, then recovered to end the month 14% higher. Results were mixed because the futures premium narrowed during the sell-off and widened again as the price recovered.

instrument: Bitcoin and Ether spot and quarterly futures; regulated and offshore venues; held to expiry, about three months
rules: Spot bought and futures sold when the annualised premium exceeds the cash rate by at least 4 points; collateral spread across at least three venues; spot held with regulated custodians where available
costs: Estimated trading fees, funding costs and bid-ask spreads on both legs deducted at each roll
constructionTitle: Strategy construction, from futures premium to venue risk limits

legs.purpose: Earns the price rise towards the futures price
Earns the premium and hedges price moves
Limits losses if a venue is unavailable in a sell-off
Meets margin calls and earns the cash rate

entry: Annualised premium at least 4 points above the cash rate
size: Set to a 6% annualised volatility target, with at most 30% of capital on one venue
exit: Position closed at expiry, or when the premium falls below the cash rate
stop: All positions reduced if any venue delays withdrawals
marketWatch: The indicators that matter are the annualised futures premium against the cash rate, open interest in futures, the share of positions held on regulated venues and the size of ETF flows. Upcoming regulatory decisions on exchange supervision and stablecoin rules, and central bank decisions that change funding costs, can alter the premium without a change in the spot price.

favourable.heading: Strong demand for leveraged exposure
favourable.text: Rising demand for leveraged long positions favours the strategy because traders pay a higher futures premium to hold exposure. In December 2020 and March 2024, steady buying lifted the premium well above the cash rate.

favourable.heading: Access through regulated venues
favourable.text: Wider access through regulated exchanges and ETFs favours the strategy because it brings steady institutional demand and reduces counterparty risk. After US spot ETFs were approved in January 2024, inflows rose and the futures premium stayed wide for about three months.

favourable.heading: Orderly rallies with stable funding
favourable.text: Orderly rallies favour the strategy because the gain on the spot position covers margin on the short futures leg, so the trade can run to expiry. In the 2020 rally, positions held to expiry earned the full premium.

adverse.heading: Exchange or custodian failure
adverse.text: A venue failure hurts the strategy because collateral can be frozen or lost even when the price hedge works. In November 2022, FTX froze withdrawals and clients lost access to assets held on the exchange.

adverse.heading: Forced liquidations in sell-offs
adverse.text: Sharp sell-offs hurt the strategy because liquidations narrow the premium and margin calls force positions to close before expiry. On 12 March 2020 bitcoin fell by more than a third in a day, and exchanges liquidated large leveraged positions.

adverse.heading: Stablecoin and funding stress
adverse.text: A loss of confidence in a stablecoin hurts the strategy because collateral and settlement depend on it, so positions cannot be moved quickly. In March 2023, USDC briefly traded near 88 cents after the failure of Silicon Valley Bank.

infoHist: Historical results show the strategy's peak-to-trough drawdown during each event, measured from its value just before the event to its lowest point using the default backtest parameters above. Each event window runs from the last market high before the shock to the market low.
infoForward: Scenario results show the estimated profit or loss over the first month of each scenario. Rehyn's scenario engine projects moves in bitcoin and ether prices, the futures premium and funding rates, which are then applied to the strategy's current spot and futures positions.
